editorial.headline: Game Equipment Manufacturing: Open Nationally, Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the making of rule-based games and related equipment, with full national PMA openness but a Bali-side block for foreign registration.
editorial.body:
KBLI 32401 is the manufacturing home for games that are built around rules, play equipment, and table-based or social play. The slim record describes a broad production activity: playing cards such as dominoes and similar cards, marbles, bekel, board games including electronic board games, chess equipment, arcade or coin-operated games, and the specialised tables and equipment used for billiards, casino games, bowling, table games, parlour games, fun-fair games, puzzles, and educational toys. In plain English, this is not the operation of a game venue. It is the industrial making of the objects and equipment used in those games.

The scale profile is unusually straightforward. Across the record, the activity is available to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the classification is not framed only for a large manufacturer; it can also describe smaller production businesses, provided the actual activity remains the making of the game tools, tables, puzzles, or equipment covered by the scope. The breadth matters because the same code can sit behind very different physical products: a small educational-toy maker, a board-game producer, or a larger manufacturer of arcade and table-game equipment can all belong here if their activity is still the manufacturing described in the record.

Nationally, the PMA picture is also clean. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives `pma_max_asing` as 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-owned company, that is the national headline: the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. There is no lower national cap in the slim record, and there is no separate national caveat to add. The correct reading is full national openness for PMA ownership, across the activity as described.

Bali is where the legal reading changes sharply. The record says `l4_bali_blocked` is true, with the reason: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026". The moratorium rule is equally direct: "Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent)". So the honest founder-facing conclusion is not that Bali has a smaller foreign-ownership percentage, a local-partner formula, or a special quota. None of those appears in the record. The conclusion is simpler and more severe: although this activity is open nationally to 100% foreign ownership, a foreigner cannot register it as a PMA activity in Bali under the Bali moratorium recorded here.
editorial.pullQuote: This is a nationally open manufacturing activity, but the Bali record turns that openness into a PMA registration block on the island.
